title: Props, every state
prompt: Paint one sheet of cut-out puppet parts for a paper-puppet film, using the attached image. Panel A is the exact layout, panel B is our footage for these props (reference: copy the object, not the photo style), panel C is the style. STYLE (panel C): flat cards cut from corrugated cardboard, gouache with confident ink linework, the flutes faintly showing through the paint, a thin raw kraft-brown cut edge round every card, brass split-pin brads; shot flat-on, even light, no shadows, no perspective. Copy the craft from C, not the clothes in it. WHAT (panel B): the props of the poem 'Resurrecting Atlantis', one row each, every state of a prop in its own cell, left to right: the relearned coin: thick translucent coin glowing faint blue with an engraved spiral (in his pinch, set on the counter, glowing in the booth tray); the admission booth: small marble-and-glass booth with a neon rim and a counter, set in the gate with two lantern-windows (queue at it, coin set down, gatekeeper nods); the elder's lantern: old brass oil lantern with a warm flame (held out leading the file, raised in the plaza); the comet / soul-light: a falling white spark with a shrinking, dimming trail of discs; the same spark becomes the beacon on the capital dome (leaving a traveller's chest, falling, landing on the dome tip, beacon); the candle: white pillar candle, flickering flame (in a lantern-window, held); the street guitar: worn acoustic guitar with painted flowers (strummed); the Tide Office notice: an enamel board on a post: 'NEXT GATES' with two times and two heights in white on blue (posted). Paint each state as a flat cardboard prop card at the size its cell gives, the same object across its row; a brass brad on the green cross (its pivot); where there is a red cross, that is where a hand grips it. LAYOUT (panel A): paint one card inside each grey ghost, in the same place, size and angle, inside its dashed outline; a brass brad exactly on every green cross; each red cross must fall inside that card's rounded end. NEVER draw a pelvis, hip, shorts or briefs card (the thighs end in a rounded seat that tucks under the hem), a sleeveless vest, lace-up boots, or sunglasses painted onto a head. OUTPUT: only the painted cards on a pure white 2048x1152 sheet laid out as panel A. Leave out panels B and C, the crosses, labels, ruler, dashed lines and ghosts.
